title: PODiff: Latent Diffusion in Proper Orthogonal Decomposition Space for Scientific Super-Resolution
claim: Operate diffusion on a small set of ordered basis coefficients, conditioned on projected inputs, then reconstruct fields and sample ensembles for uncertainty.
layout: Multi-box flow: input left, diffusion center, outputs right; math under each stage
description: A multi-box pipeline diagram with rounded panels and arrows. At top left, a red-bordered low-resolution temperature field (x_LR) is shown. A downward arrow labeled fixed upsampling and projection on POD basis leads to a conditioning vector panel, which has a descending bar chart of coefficients (K << d). An orange arrow connects it to the central panel, which shows the denoising network (epsilon_theta) and a residual MLP drawn as a neural-net graph. Above it, a forward diffusion panel shows a chain a0→a1→a2→…→aT with the noising equation. A thick black arrow points from the forward process down to the reverse denoising panel. At right, an uncertainty quantification box describes multiple predicted samples and their reconstruction. Below it are a red-bordered high-resolution reconstructed sample field and a reconstruct equation box. The figure uses blue and red field images, black text and equations, and orange arrows.
caption: PODiff: conditional diffusion in a POD latent space. Low-resolution inputs are upsampled and projected onto a truncated POD basis to condition a diffusion model operating on POD coefficients. Reverse diffusion samples are reconstructed via the POD basis, yielding ensembles of high-resolution fields for uncertainty quantification.
abstract: Probabilistic super-resolution of high-dimensional spatial fields using diffusion models is often computationally prohibitive due to the cost of operating directly in pixel space. We propose PODiff, a structured conditional generative framework that performs diffusion in a fixed, variance-ordered Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) coefficient space, exploiting the orthogonality of POD modes to impose an interpretable, variance-ordered latent geometry. This design enables efficient ensemble generation, preserves dominant spatial structure, and yields spatially interpretable, well-calibrated uncertainty at substantially lower computational cost. We evaluate PODiff on sea surface temperature downscaling over the West Australian coast and on a controlled advection-diffusion benchmark. PODiff achieves reconstruction accuracy comparable to pixel-space diffusion while requiring significantly less memory and producing more reliable uncertainty estimates than deterministic and Monte Carlo Dropout baselines.
